inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL UPDATE JOIN derives one latest related record per entity through a grouped MAX date subquery and writes the resulting owner into the entity table.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one unit with two owner events and one unit with no event. The grouped latest-owner join updates only the unit with an event.

fixture_notes: Unit 3101 receives owner 52 from its latest event; unit 3102 retains its NULL owner because it has no event.
determinism_notes: The single unit has one event on its maximum day. All IDs, dates, and owners are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE asset_units_min (unit_id INT PRIMARY KEY, unit_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, owner_id INT NULL)
CREATE TABLE asset_owner_events_min (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, unit_id INT NOT NULL, owner_id INT NOT NULL, event_day INT NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO asset_units_min VALUES (3101, 'north bay', NULL), (3102, 'south bay', NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE asset_units_min AS u JOIN (SELECT e.unit_id, e.owner_id FROM asset_owner_events_min AS e JOIN (SELECT unit_id, MAX(event_day) AS latest_day FROM asset_owner_events_min GROUP BY unit_id) AS latest ON e.unit_id = latest.unit_id AND e.event_day = latest.latest_day) AS latest_owner ON u.unit_id = latest_owner.unit_id SET u.owner_id = latest_owner.owner_id

checks.sql: SELECT unit_id, unit_name, owner_id FROM asset_units_min ORDER BY unit_id
SELECT event_id, unit_id, owner_id, event_day FROM asset_owner_events_min ORDER BY event_id
